title: Flu Season Arrives Early — and Texas Is Among the Hardest-Hit States

content:
Flu season has arrived early in the United States — and Texas is among the states where it is hitting hardest, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The CDC's weekly FluView report for the week ending Nov. 7, published Nov. 13, found outpatient visits for flu-like illness at 3.2%, above the 2.9% national baseline, and flu test positivity at 11.3%, up from 9.1% the week before.

Flu activity is now high or very high in seven states: California, Louisiana, Oregon, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas and Washington. The dominant virus is influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, which made up 98.9% of the influenza A viruses subtyped that week.

The CDC estimates at least 2.6 million illnesses, 36,000 hospitalizations and 2,100 deaths from flu so far this season. Five children have died of flu this season, including two deaths reported in the latest week. The CDC notes that child deaths are often reported weeks after they occur, so the count may rise.

The agency said this early-season activity is higher than typically observed at this time of year, but cautioned that an earlier increase does not necessarily lead to a higher seasonal peak or greater overall severity. Its preliminary assessment rates the season's severity as low across all age groups so far.

CDC forecasts predict a likely increase in flu hospital admissions and emergency department visits for flu in the week ending Nov. 28 — the week of Thanksgiving gatherings and travel.

Sources:

  • Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, FluView, week ending Nov. 7, 2026
  • Medical Xpress (CIDRAP), Nov. 16, 2026
